name: custom-source-abort
purpose: The caller cancels mid-stream against the CUSTOM OpenAI-compatible source: the backend must tear the upstream connection down, which the recorder observes as a client disconnect. The custom source takes its URL and key from the REQUEST, so this case also proves cancellation is not implemented only for the sources that carry a seam.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; presence and scheme are the contract, the value is not.

tier2.rule: the mock authority is replaced with <mock> before hashing
tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend. The rest of the body is compared byte for byte through the digest.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
